title: Audit reports new LLM hallucinations in accepted NeurIPS 2025 papers
source_title: GPTZero finds 100 new hallucinations in NeurIPS 2025 accepted papers
summary: A hallucination-detection firm reports finding 100 new hallucinations in papers accepted at NeurIPS 2025, prompting discussion of how fabricated content reaches peer-reviewed venues.

title: Military close call linked to AI-hallucinated intelligence report
source_title: US Military had close call after using AI for hallucinated intelligence report
summary: A news report links a US military close call to an AI system that produced a hallucinated intelligence report, illustrating the stakes when fabricated output enters decision-making.

title: Essay argues code hallucinations are the least dangerous LLM error
source_title: Hallucinations in code are the least dangerous form of LLM mistakes
summary: An essay argues hallucinated code is the least dangerous LLM error because it typically fails when executed, so harder-to-verify hallucinations deserve more attention.

title: Paper argues hallucination is an innate limit of large language models
source_title: Hallucination is inevitable: An innate limitation of large language models
summary: A paper argues that hallucination is an innate limitation of large language models rather than a temporary bug; the discussion weighs whether mitigations can remove it.

title: Semantic entropy proposed as a detector for LLM hallucinations
source_title: Detecting hallucinations in large language models using semantic entropy
summary: A Nature paper reports a semantic-entropy method for detecting hallucinations in LLM outputs; the thread discusses what such detection implies for trustworthy deployment.

title: Explainer examines why LLMs fabricate and how to mitigate it
source_title: AI hallucinations: Why LLMs make things up (and how to fix it)
summary: A vendor explainer reviews why large language models make things up and surveys mitigation options; commenters debate root causes and the limits of each fix.

title: Benchmark measures how often models repeat human falsehoods
source_title: TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods
quote: We propose a benchmark to measure whether a language model is truthful in generating answers to questions.
summary: TruthfulQA introduces 817 questions across 38 categories that elicit false answers learned from human text; the best tested model was truthful 58% of the time versus 94% for humans.

title: Survey organizes hallucination measurement and mitigation in NLG
source_title: Survey of Hallucination in Natural Language Generation
quote: In this survey, we thus provide a broad overview of the research progress and challenges in the hallucination problem in NLG.
summary: A comprehensive survey of hallucination in natural language generation, covering metrics, mitigation methods, task-specific progress, and hallucinations in large language models.

title: Hallucinated citations found in accepted top-tier conference papers
source_title: Phantom References: Hallucinated Citations That Survive Peer Review at Top-Tier Conferences
quote: in 2025, roughly one in twenty NeurIPS and USENIX Security papers contains at least two likely hallucinated academic-paper-like references under our strict definition
summary: An audit of accepted ICLR, ICML, NeurIPS and USENIX Security papers finds hallucinated citations have entered the archival record, including award-winning papers; peer review alone did not prevent it.

title: Citation fabrication traced to field-specific neurons in LLMs
source_title: Where Fake Citations Are Made: Tracing Field-Level Hallucination to Specific Neurons in LLMs
quote: LLMs frequently generate fictitious yet convincing citations, often expressing high confidence even when the underlying reference is wrong.
summary: Across 9 models and 108,000 generated references, author names failed most often; researchers identify field-specific hallucination neurons in Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct and show causal interventions change fabrication rates.

title: Coding-agent users report frequent hallucinated assumptions about project files
summary: Claude Code bug report says that after a model upgrade the assistant hallucinates more often: it skips reading the mapped resource files and assumes project details from thin information instead of checking them.
notes: GitHub issue state=open at collection time; metrics from unauthenticated search API.

title: Search-product users report fabricated facts and a paraphrase presented as a quote
summary: Kagi Kite issue reports that a part of the generated overview information is hallucinated with no source to back it up, and that a paraphrase of a source is presented as if it were a direct quote.
notes: GitHub issue state=open at collection time; metrics from unauthenticated search API.
